Rep.  BY THE PP, ASSAM Advocate for the Petitioner : MD S ALI Advocate for the Respondent : PP, ASSAM  BEFORE  HONOURABLE MRS. JUSTICE SUSMITA PHUKAN KHAUND
ORDER Date : 15-12-2023 Heard Mr. S. Ali, learned counsel for the petitioner Bipul Kr. Koch @ Bubai.

The petitioner has filed this application under 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking for quashing of the impugned order dated 06.07.2023 and the subsequent orders by the learned Sessions Judge, Sonitpur, Tezpur, in Page No.# 2/3 Sessions Case No. 88/2023 issuing NBWA against the petitioner.

sentences.text: Also heard Mr. K.K. Das, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State of Assam/respondent No. 1.
The learned Additional Public Prosecutor has accepted notice on behalf of the respondent No.1, so no formal notice is required to be issued to the respondent No. 1.
However, sufficient copies be furnished during the course of the day.
I have considered the submissions at the bar.
The petitioner is booked under Section 376/511 of the Indian Penal Code.
He is willing to cooperate with the trial.
The charges are yet to be framed.
The NBWA was issued against the petitioner because the petitioner was absent without steps.

It is submitted that due to a misunderstanding the learned counsel for the petitioner stated in the petition No. 1539/2023 dated 06.07.2023 before the trial Court, that the learned counsel was unable to communicate with the present petitioner.
It is due to a misunderstanding that the learned counsel for the petitioner could not communicate with the petitioner.
It is submitted that the petitioner's mobile phone was damaged and so the learned counsel was unable to communicate with him.
It is also submitted that on the last date he could not appear as his daughter was unwell.
The petitioner who is apprehending arrest has prayed to quash the order dated 06.07.2023 and subsequent orders of issuance of warrant.
I have considered the submissions that the petitioner is willing to cooperate with the trial.
I have taken a pragmatic view as the petitioner has pledged that he will never default appearance.
Considering the submissions at the bar, the NBWA is kept in abeyance up- to 05.01.2024.

The petitioner is directed to appear before the trial Court within Page No.# 3/3 a period of fifteen days and apply for regular bail which may be considered by the trial Court as per the merits of the case.
Criminal Petition stands closed in the above terms.
